newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says it did not fire rockets at Israel.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says it did not fire rockets at Israel.

text.p: Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah said on Friday it has not launched any Katyusha rockets into northern Israel.
"We the Islamic reistance deny firmly that we have launched any Katyusha rockets on Friday," a Hizbollah official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
Officials of three radical Palestinian guerrilla factions in Lebanon contacted by Reuters also said they had not carried out any rocket attacks on northern Israel.

The Israeli army said Katyusha rockets slammed into the Western Galilee region of northern Israel earlier on Friday at about 8 pm (1800 gmt) from Qlaileh area of southern Lebanon. There were no reports of casualties or damage, it said.

Hizbollah -- which followed a policy of firing Katyusha rockets into Israel whenever Israeli shelling caused Lebanese civilian casualties -- has refrained from such attacks under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April.

Earlier on Friday, Hizbollah MP Mohammad Fneish said the group was "dissatisfied" with a statement by a five-nation ceasefire monitors, which held Israel responsible for the injury of Lebanese civilians on Saturday. The monitors had said they deplored the injuries caused by the bombardment.
